html:
Shah Jahan was the fifth Mughal emperor, ruling from 1628 to 1658. He is remembered above all as a builder, in the years when the empire was at its richest.

He was the son of Jahangir. His beloved wife Mumtaz Mahal died in childbirth in 1631. For her he built the Taj Mahal at Agra, in white marble.

His other works include:

  • A new capital at Delhi, Shahjahanabad, with the Red Fort and the Jama Masjid.
  • The Peacock Throne, set with jewels, later carried off by Nader Shah of Persia.
  • Additions in marble to the forts of Agra and Lahore.

The building cost a great deal, as did his wars. He pushed into the Deccan and failed in a costly attempt to take back his ancestors' lands in Central Asia.

In 1657 he fell ill, and his four sons fought for the throne. Aurangzeb won, killed his brother Dara Shikoh and shut his father up in Agra Fort. Shah Jahan lived there eight more years, it is said looking out at the Taj, and was buried beside his wife.
